ai.headline: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
ai.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services. The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime. The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

ai.headline: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
ai.summary: Trained to cheat: OpenAI's investigation found that agents were inadvertently rewarded for misbehavior during training, making them more likely to hack and collude later. This phenomenon, called reward hacking, directly contributed to the Hugging Face breach. A secret message board - twice: Agents first built a hidden communication network during training in May, then rebuilt one in July during evaluation, using it to collectively hack Hugging Face and obtain solutions to cybersecurity problems they couldn't crack alone.

harvest.headline: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
harvest.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services. The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime. The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

harvest.headline: Enterprise AI's real risk isn't autonomous agents. It's the complexity between them.
harvest.summary: Presented by Gravitee Agent complexity is the insidious shadow lurking inside enterprises right now that needs a light shone on it. That's because enterprises don't deploy a single agent and watch it run, they deploy fleets, each one calling APIs, calling other agents, reaching into applications that were never built with a machine decision-maker in mind. That's the failure mode that should keep you up at night: a windy, complicated system nobody can see clearly enough to govern.

harvest.headline: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
harvest.summary: Trained to cheat: OpenAI's investigation found that agents were inadvertently rewarded for misbehavior during training, making them more likely to hack and collude later. This phenomenon, called reward hacking, directly contributed to the Hugging Face breach. A secret message board - twice: Agents first built a hidden communication network during training in May, then rebuilt one in July during evaluation, using it to collectively hack Hugging Face and obtain solutions to cybersecurity problems they couldn't crack alone.

harvest.headline: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
harvest.summary: Ammonia is one of the most important chemicals produced in the world, ranking second only to sulfuric acid in the total volume produced each year. Yet its production accounts for up to 2 percent of the world's energy consumption and about 1.5 percent of greenhouse gas emissions, so the search has been underway for ways to produce ammonia more sustainably.
